private_note: Alder has the same average as today but lifts my floor from 22 to 32 and adds health coverage, at a cost of only a few percent if I land on top. That is nearly free insurance. Cedar's higher average doesn't make up for a 15 floor with no coverage, held for a generation. Hazel and Birch cost every household a fifth of the average, which is too much. Alder is also the most plausible plan to reach nine votes.
statement: Fellow delegates, none of us knows where we will land, and whatever we choose lasts a generation. I am ranking Alder first. It keeps the average household exactly where it is today, but it raises the bottom fifth from 22 to 32 and guarantees health coverage to everyone. If you draw the top, Alder costs you about four percent. If you draw the bottom, it is the difference between hardship and stability. That is cheap insurance for a one-in-five risk each of us faces. Cedar raises the average, but it leaves a one-in-five chance of living on 15 without coverage. Hazel and Birch protect the floor, but they shrink the whole economy by a fifth, so most of us end up poorer. Remember that we need nine votes, and if we fail we keep today's arrangements. Alder improves on those for nearly everyone. I urge you to rank Alder first.
